clue.text: Second target for golfer in dispute

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
par is the score a golfer aims for on a hole

explanation.surface: A golfer's second shot target is in dispute, perhaps a row over the course.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or exchange blows, so it is a verb synonym of dispute.

clue.text: Recording supremo mixed record up

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters are jumbled together, as on a mixing desk

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A studio boss has mixed a record and it is coming up the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' fits the studio picture so well that it reads as sound engineering, not as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A record producer is the person in charge of a recording session, hence its supremo.

clue.text: Irrational charge for thief

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
a rate is a price or fee charged

explanation.surface: An unreasonable fee seems fit for a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' reads as unreasonable; in maths an irrational number like pi cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber at sea, or someone who steals copyright work, so a kind of thief.

clue.text: Lack of interest in American way finally at an end

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
a path is a way or route

indicators.note: at an end points to the closing letter only of the word just before it

parts.note: the last letter of the word itself

explanation.surface: Indifference in the American way of life is finally over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like the indicator acting on 'way', but it is itself the source word; 'at an end' takes its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference: an absence of enthusiasm or concern for anything.

clue.text: Settled 12 forgetting each name in disarray

indicators.note: something in disarray is disordered, so the remaining letters are shuffled
to forget every one of something is to leave them all out, so each such letter is dropped

parts.note: the answer to 12 across
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A matter was settled despite risk, every name forgotten in the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: ENDANGER holds two Ns, and 'each name' tells you to remove both, leaving EDAGER to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed, as an adjective, means decided upon or fixed by consent, as an agreed price is a settled one.

clue.text: First person taken in by Nostradamus

indicators.note: something taken in by a word is held inside it, so read within the name that follows

parts.note: letters three to six of the prophet's name

explanation.surface: The first person to be fooled by the famous French prophet's predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Adam is the first man God created, so the first human being.

clue.text: A-ha flyer distributed for six months

indicators.note: distributed means handed out in different directions, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Leaflets for the Norwegian band A-ha were handed out over six months.
explanation.walkthrough: A-ha were a Norwegian pop band of the 1980s, so the flyer looks like gig publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Half a year of twelve months is a period of six months.

clue.text: Vocally perform around eg Bristol fair

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps itself about the other

parts.note: to sing is to perform with the voice
Bristol is an English port city

explanation.surface: An instruction to sing around Bristol's fair, perhaps a busker's tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a noun, a funfair in Bristol, but it is the adjective for playing by the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting behaviour is generous and decent, as a good sport would be, so fair-minded.

clue.text: Genuinely get better, taking drug

indicators.note: taking means accepting something into itself, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to rally is to recover, as a patient or a market does
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone truly recovers while on medication.
explanation.definitionFit: Really is an adverb meaning truly or in fact, the same as genuinely.

clue.text: Doctor argued at former student

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A physician quarrelled with an alumnus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person, an academic title even, but it is the verb meaning to falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduate has completed a degree, so is someone who used to be a student.

clue.text: Elegant welcome in Cricket Club

indicators.note: in places the greeting inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: CC is the standard abbreviation for Cricket Club
hi is a word of greeting

explanation.surface: A stylish reception at the cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a French loan word for stylish and fashionable.

clue.text: Male with a rubbish skin condition

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
'with' joins the article on
trash is rubbish

explanation.surface: A man with a dreadful skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat rash is prickly heat, a red itchy eruption caused by blocked sweat glands.

clue.text: Gender somehow comprises a new risk

indicators.note: to comprise is to include, so the reworked word holds the following letters
somehow says the word is rearranged in some unspecified way

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Gender somehow brings a fresh hazard, a remark about modern politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risk' looks like a noun, a new risk, but it is the verb: to endanger is to put at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to expose it to harm, the verb sense of risk.

clue.text: Harry Nilsson always grates at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the initials of the three words

explanation.surface: The singer Harry Nilsson always irritates people from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Nilsson was an American singer; his first name is the definition, used as a verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to harass them persistently, which is what nagging does.

clue.text: Now Morse changed where investigations are written up?

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse has changed, now writing up his detective cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is the Oxford detective of novels and TV, so 'investigations' suggests police work; the question mark flags that it is journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsroom is the office where reporters turn their inquiries into published stories.

clue.text: March Madness involving one union

parts.note: Mar is the calendar abbreviation for March

indicators.note: involving means including, so the second piece takes in another

parts.note: rage is fury, a kind of madness
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The American college basketball frenzy known as March Madness includes one union.
explanation.walkthrough: March Madness is the name for the US college basketball tournament, which makes the two words look like one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is the formal joining of two people, a union in the wedding sense.

clue.text: A group of whales, almost entirely lacking pelvic fins?

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the final letter of the next word is cut

parts.note: taken as written
a pod is the collective noun for whales
all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A group of whales, nearly all of them, without pelvic fins.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a specialist one: apodal fish, such as eels, have no pelvic fins.
explanation.definitionFit: Apodal means footless; of fish it describes those without ventral fins, from Greek for no feet.

clue.text: Lead on English books on reserve

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
ice means reserve, coolness of manner; 'on' joins it to what comes before

explanation.surface: Leading the English book collection that is kept in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead on' sounds like an instruction to go ahead, but it means to tempt someone along.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt, and to lead someone on is to tempt or beguile them.

clue.text: Either side of weapon is tatty

indicators.note: each side of a word is its outermost letter, so take the two ends

parts.note: its first and last letters, which sit on either side
'either ... or' pairs off, so the word stands for or

explanation.surface: Both sides of a weapon look shabby and battered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either side' reads as one phrase, but either gives OR, and the sides of the weapon sit around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn clothes or furniture are threadbare from use, which is what tatty means.

clue.text: Photograph me too!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the cry when two things match, from the card game

explanation.walkthrough: Snap is a children's card game where you shout when two matching cards appear, so it is said when you share something with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal photograph, and Snap! is exclaimed on finding a match.

clue.text: Eruption, but Korea rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together again differently, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A volcano erupted, but Korea was rebuilt afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak is a sudden flare-up, of war or disease, just as an eruption is.

clue.text: State found between Pennsylvania and Vermont

indicators.note: found between asks for the letters lying at the meeting point of the two names, ignoring the joining word

parts.note: the closing letter of the first state
the opening three letters of the second state, the end nearest the first

explanation.surface: A US state lying between Pennsylvania and Vermont.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the join of the two state names once the word between them is skipped. With two states named, 'State' looks like a noun such as New York; it is the verb meaning to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare firmly, the verb sense of state.

clue.text: Flipping like some old socks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mild curse, a polite substitute for damned
second meaning: mended with needle and wool

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' is British slang used as a mild swear word, as in 'flipping cheek'.
explanation.definitionFit: Darned is a euphemistic intensifier like flipping, and darned socks have had holes repaired by stitching.

clue.text: Firm at sea also welcomes task

indicators.note: something that welcomes another takes it inside

parts.note: and means also, in addition
a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A company in crisis also takes on a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm at sea' suggests a confused business, but read literally it is a ship held fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is anchored is held fixed in place on the water, so stable while afloat.

clue.text: Fellow extremely evangelical in place of worship

parts.note: a chap is a man, a fellow

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two end letters of the following word

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man who is extremely evangelical in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small church or a room for prayer, a place of worship.
